Best effort: this build requires wireless debugging to be turned off manually

Pigu will leave Android's wireless debugging switch enabled after it connects.

• The ADB port stays open while wireless debugging is on.
• Any device on the same network with your ADB key can try to connect.
• Android keeps the wireless debugging notification visible.
• This increases the attack surface and may use more battery.

Use it only on networks you trust, and turn it off when you no longer need it. When this is off, Pigu turns wireless debugging off again after connecting.

Start Pigu to change this setting

Android 12 and newer can kill Pigu's shell process as a “phantom process” when the device is under memory pressure.

Disabling the limit may keep Pigu running, but it changes a global setting for every app. It can increase battery use and let runaway background processes continue. It does not override an OEM's own process manager, and it may not survive an Android update.

You can restore Android's default from this screen at any time.
